name: Malden
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Malden, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Malden, MA: the Fellsmere Pond tree lighting, neighborhood lightings, Breakfast with Santa at the Moose and library fun.
lede: Malden celebrates neighborhood by neighborhood, led by the tree lighting at Fellsmere Pond, with Santa breakfasts and library programs through December.
celebrates: Malden marks the season with several neighborhood lightings. The city calendar lists a tree lighting at Fellsmere Pond, a Maplewood Square lighting hosted by the Ward 6 councillor with hot chocolate and refreshments from the Maplewood Association, and a Ward 7 lighting at Lincoln Commons and Anderson Field with hot chocolate and cookies. Malden City Hall hosts a public menorah lighting as well. Community groups add Santa visits, such as the Frank Says Hi breakfast at the Malden Moose on Broadway, and the Malden Public Library on Salem Street schedules holiday movie nights and cookie decorating for teens.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Malden lit the Fellsmere Pond holiday tree on Saturday, November 29, at 4 pm, and the Malden Advocate covered it as the 15th annual Christmas tree lighting at Fellsmere Pond. Earlier city calendar listings described the Fellsmere lighting as free and open to all, with music, hot chocolate and a visit from Santa, and the city has collected new toys and food there for local holiday drives.
facts: Malden sits on hilly land north of the Mystic River and was settled by Puritans in 1640. It became a separate town in 1649 under the name Mauldon. At the time of the American Revolution about 1,000 people lived there, and they were early to resist British rule. Adoniram Judson, the first Protestant missionary in Burma, came from Malden. Neighboring Everett was part of Malden until it separated in 1870.
trains: Malden is on the MBTA Orange Line, with stops at Malden Center and Oak Grove, the line's northern end, so a ride into Boston to see the downtown holiday lights is simple. Malden Center is also a stop on the Haverhill Line commuter rail from North Station. For a Christmas train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a holiday train through the lights, and the Boston Street Railway Association shares the history of Boston's streetcars.

kidfact: When Malden became a town in 1649, its name was spelled Mauldon. Can you spot the letters that changed?
faq: Where is the Malden tree lighting?

Malden's main lighting is at Fellsmere Pond, at West Border Road and Savin Street. The city calendar also lists neighborhood lightings in Maplewood Square and at Lincoln Commons and Anderson Field in Ward 7. The Fellsmere lighting has fallen on the Saturday after Thanksgiving in the late afternoon, with music, hot chocolate and Santa.
Is the Fellsmere Pond tree lighting free?

Past City of Malden calendar listings described the Fellsmere Pond lighting as free and open to all, and the city has streamed it live on its Facebook page. Check the city calendar each fall for the current listing, since the details for each season are posted shortly before the lighting.
How do we get to Malden by train?

Take the Orange Line to Malden Center or Oak Grove, or ride the Haverhill Line commuter rail from North Station to Malden Center. Malden Center is downtown, near Malden City Hall and the Malden Public Library on Salem Street, so it works well for events in the center of the city.
Are there Santa breakfasts in Malden?

Yes. The Frank Says Hi charity holds a Breakfast with Santa at the Malden Moose at 562 Broadway, with breakfast, pictures with Santa, crafts and raffles. Money raised goes to the Frank Says Hi Scholarship Foundation, and the host has sold tickets at the door with a lower price for kids.
